segments.t: Rival talent agent François Bréhier ambushes Andréa Martel and Fabrice Luchini at their dinner table. Hoping to steal Luchini back, Bréhier reveals that the coveted James Bond audition was an elaborate trick orchestrated by ASK. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Ne te laisse pas avoir, Fabrice!
Cette femme est très dangereuse.
Pardon? De quoi est-ce que tu parles?
L'histoire du film Bond était du bidon!
C'est Andréa qui a tout manigancé.
Je n'ai pas le pouvoir d'inventer ça.
Ce n'était pas la vraie directrice de casting.
Mais alors, qui était cette femme?
Elle voulait se venger de notre agence.
C'est vous qui avez appelé le fisc!
Votre agence est complètement ruinée!
Crois ce que tu veux, Fabrice.
Vous êtes vraiment bizarres, vous les agents!
Fiche-moi la paix, François!
Now let's break down the scene step by step. Listen to each line, followed by its meaning and a short explanation.
Ne te laisse pas avoir, Fabrice!
'Do not let yourself be fooled, Fabrice!' François bursts in with a negative casual command meaning 'do not let yourself'. A nice sentence in French.
Cette femme est très dangereuse.
'This woman is very dangerous.' He attacks with a clear cognate, carrying an extra sound at the end because it describes a female. A great expression in French.
Pardon? De quoi est-ce que tu parles?
'Excuse me? What are you talking about?' Fabrice is shocked, using a handy chunk that literally asks 'of what do you speak'. You can say this in French.
L'histoire du film Bond était du bidon!
'The Bond film story was total nonsense!' François uses an informal everyday expression meaning 'nonsense' or 'phony'. In French, this is widely used.
C'est Andréa qui a tout manigancé.
'It is Andréa who engineered everything.' He points fingers by building from 'it is', followed by her name and 'who'. The French love this expression.
Je n'ai pas le pouvoir d'inventer ça.
'I do not have the power to make that up.' In the negative, Andréa's action meaning 'have' is surrounded by two small pieces. In French, it fits perfectly.
Ce n'était pas la vraie directrice de casting.
'It was not the real casting director.' François uses a past description meaning 'it was not', pointing out the fake. A nice way to say it in French.
Mais alors, qui était cette femme?
'Well then, who was this woman?' Fabrice questions the trickery using a handy chunk meaning 'well then' or 'but then'. In French, it is a great choice.
Elle voulait se venger de notre agence.
'She wanted to get revenge on our agency.' The rival explains the motive with a past action meaning 'she wanted'. The French find this natural.
C'est vous qui avez appelé le fisc!
'It is you who called the tax inspectors!' Andréa fires back using the formal 'you' to show distance and anger. In French, this sounds very fluent.
Votre agence est complètement ruinée!
'Your agency is completely ruined!' He sneers at their financial state, pairing a cognate with 'completely'. The French use this structure often.
Crois ce que tu veux, Fabrice.
'Believe what you want, Fabrice.' She dismisses the debate with a casual command to 'believe', followed by 'what you want'. In French, this phrasing is common.
Vous êtes vraiment bizarres, vous les agents!
'You agents are really strange!' Fabrice shows his disgust by using the plural 'you', joined by a cognate meaning 'bizarre'. You will find this useful in French.
Fiche-moi la paix, François!

'Léave me alone, François!' Andréa shuts him down entirely with a strong colloquial idiom for telling someone to back off. This sounds extremely natural in French. Now let's listen to the entire exchange once more from beginning to end.
Ne te laisse pas avoir, Fabrice!
Cette femme est très dangereuse.
Pardon? De quoi est-ce que tu parles?
L'histoire du film Bond était du bidon!
C'est Andréa qui a tout manigancé.
Je n'ai pas le pouvoir d'inventer ça.
Ce n'était pas la vraie directrice de casting.
Mais alors, qui était cette femme?
Elle voulait se venger de notre agence.
C'est vous qui avez appelé le fisc!
Votre agence est complètement ruinée!
Crois ce que tu veux, Fabrice.
Vous êtes vraiment bizarres, vous les agents!
Fiche-moi la paix, François!

François Bréhier exposes the James Bond audition ruse, leaving Fabrice thoroughly bewildered. Remember the forceful conversational French phrase for telling someone to back off: fiche-moi la paix. See you next time!
Bonne soirée!
